Steam is required at the water gas shift area and the carbon capture island reboiler heat exchanger. And power is primarily needed for BF gas compression, CO compression, and other auxiliary facilities. The 2 steam and power requirement for the project is mentioned below. a) Steam: 1,332 MMBtu/hr. b) Power: 73 MW 2.0 Sourcing Option Study for Steam and Electricity Multiple options have been evaluated for sourcing steam and power (specifically waste heat recovery options to minimize secondary emissions and cost reductions). The possible options, along with outcomes, are as follows: a) 15 PSI steam from existing powerhouse: The existing powerhouse also generates 15 PSI steam which is presently available. However, it has not been considered for the project for the following reasons: i. The generation of 15 PSI steam is inconsistent, but the project needs consistent (continuous and of specific quality) steam. ii. 15 PSI steam's heat duty is insufficient for the carbon capture unit reboiler. Thus, it cannot be used in the reboiler. iii. The water gas shift process needs 60 PSI steam. Therefore, 15 PSI steam could not be considered for the water gas shift process. iv. The generated quantity of 15 PSI steam is much lesser than the requirement considering the overall steam requirement for the project. b) Sourcing steam from BOF waste gas: The potential of generating steam from the BOF waste gas project has also been evaluated. However, the demand for steel production at Burns Harbor drives the BOF operation, and the situation may arise when the blast furnace is running. During this situation, the waste gas steam cannot be made available. Therefore, considering the inconsistency in availability, this option is not considered for the project for sourcing steam. c) Biomass-based boiler: Biomass-fed boilers also have been evaluated for sourcing steam and power to avoid secondary emissions. The scale of operation for sourcing, handling, and processing biomass is an issue for a 2.8 mtpa CO capture unit. Therefore, biomass boiler has 2 not been considered for further evaluation. d) Installation of coke dry quenching facilities: The Burns Harbor steel plant has coke ovens with wet quenching facilities. It has been evaluated if coke dry quenching facilities can be installed to generate the required steam. The coke dry quenching facility offers multiple benefits over the wet quenching facility. • Sensible heat from coke can be used to produce high-grade steam • Moisture in coke is reduced significantly, leading to better BF coke quality and a reduction in the coke rate Attachment-1: Steam & Electricity Sourcing Study 4 DE-FE0031937 / 0002 250 PSI steam can be generated from the dry quenching of coke (near the existing coke oven) and can be transferred to the project site through the existing steam network of 250 PSI. Additionally, about 9 MW of power can be produced by a back-pressure turbine due to the conversion of high-pressure steam to low-pressure steam required for the project. However, this can not match the total steam and power requirement.
